A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BT-σ study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on SummEval and Topical-Chat, including aggregation performance, method variants, and analyses of judge reliability and cycle inconsistency.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds NovelEval results, a Crowd-BT comparison, jury-size experiments, and statistical significance reporting.

M1.justification: BT-σ, BT-σ-asp, hard BT-σ, and probability symmetrisation are retained. V2 explicitly writes the joint likelihood and discloses optimization details, but does not establish a change to the proposed aggregation procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds question-to-passage relevance assessment on NovelEval, extending coverage beyond summarisation and dialogue evaluation. This is a distinct evaluation task, although the reported experiment uses only 7 of its 21 queries (Appendix C).

E2.justification: V2 adds Crowd-BT as an evaluated reliability-aware comparator on SummEval (Figure 3a and Section 5.2). It explicitly does not report Crowd-BT on Topical-Chat. The existing comparator sets in the retained experiments remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols select 7 NovelEval queries by excluding near-zero Avg-Prob SRC cases and evaluate representative judge subsets of sizes 2–8. Appendix D also changes the stated probability-extraction tokens from yes/no to A/B, matching the retained prompts; this reported correction does not establish that experiments were rerun. Existing complete-pair comparisons and SRC averaging are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix B.4 adds a substantive jury-size sensitivity analysis, testing aggregation with 2–8 judges. Section 3.2 additionally reports a qualitative check relating four-cycle and three-cycle rates, without numerical correlations. Appendix C adds judge-performance and inconsistency analyses on NovelEval; the earlier aspect-specific and hard-versus-soft analyses remain.

E5.justification: V2 first reports significance tests against Avg-Prob, including p < 0.001 for SummEval COH/CON and p < 0.05 for FLU/REL, attributed to hard BT-σ. Topical-Chat findings are described as mixed. The test procedure, repeated-run counts, and seeds remain unspecified.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their numerical results. Additions include Crowd-BT's SummEval SRC of 48.35, jury-size results, and NovelEval SRC of 46.92 for BT-σ versus 45.28 for soft BT and 43.59 for Avg-Prob (Table 8). The new eight-judge BT-σ entry of 59.92 in Table 6 conflicts with the retained 59.84 in Figure 3b, without an explained setting difference.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds the mathematical assertion that higher-order cycles decompose into three-cycles, providing an additional justification for the chosen analysis without supplying a proof. The expanded hard-BT and BT-σ likelihood displays otherwise restate the existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about inconsistency, unsupervised reliability-aware aggregation, performance benefits, and interpretable discriminators. The added experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds a logits-access limitation and develops the biased-majority limitation beyond v1's brief impact statement. Section 3.3 qualifies the calibration analogy. Appendix B.4 adds jury-size robustness interpretations, but its universal outperformance claim exceeds Table 6: with three judges, BT-σ scores 58.90 versus soft BT's 58.96.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies SciPy L-BFGS-B optimization, uniform initialization over [0,1), and typical convergence within 100 iterations. It also corrects the documented extraction tokens to A/B. These improve implementation documentation; the NovelEval prompt and exact retained-query identifiers are still absent.

R1.justification: V2 positions BT-σ against Crowd-BT, distinguishing binary mixture-based reliability from its soft-probability formulation. It adds references for Crowd-BT, NovelEval, and L-BFGS-B. Updates to existing preprint/publication records and Qwen authorship do not constitute new related works.

P1.justification: V2 consolidates baseline descriptions in Section 4, adds implementation and limitations subsections, expands appendix explanations, and moves the prompts appendix from C to D. Local language and bibliographic edits accompany these changes, while the overall narrative and most retained prose remain stable.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 6–8 and NovelEval Figures 9–10, and inserts a Crowd-BT bar into Figure 3a. V1's Topical-Chat Figures 8 and 9 become two panels of v2's Figure 8. Existing visual data are otherwise retained, with localized resizing, caption shortening, and repositioning.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility through optimizer details and corrected token documentation, adds a relevant Crowd-BT comparison, and states concrete applicability limits. The additional validation is less conclusive than advertised: NovelEval selects 7/21 queries using baseline performance, significance procedures are unspecified, and Table 6 conflicts with some accompanying claims and retained results. These weaknesses limit the gains, but the clearer documentation and expanded comparison support a modest net improvement.
